caption: 01 · ASK — Can the question change the work?. Frame a bounded design or institutional question, a decision date, relevant communities, and evidence that would require revision. “Inspiration” is too broad to audit.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping can the question change the work? within The Independent Designer’s Research Department.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 02 · SOURCE — Can each reference be recovered?. Preserve creator, title, date, institution, identifier, canonical URL, access date, rights statement, excerpt limits, and local notes. Keep link-only records visible without copying restricted media.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping can each reference be recovered? within The Independent Designer’s Research Department.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 03 · INTERPRET — Where does fact end and judgment begin?. Write source description, studio inference, transformation, disagreement, and cultural-authority question in separate fields. This prevents an appealing object from being made to prove more than its record supports.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping where does fact end and judgment begin? within The Independent Designer’s Research Department.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 04 · RETURN — What did research change?. Attach the altered silhouette, material, process, refusal, claim, credit, or archive rule to the source trail. If nothing changed, record why the reference was rejected rather than laundering it into a mood board.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins

caption: Formal research systems can privilege institutions that already catalogued their holdings and marginalize living, oral, community, or embodied knowledge. Rigor must include consent, compensation, cultural review, and the right not to extract—not only better metadata.
